title: Reproducing Long et al. 2012: where the germanium goes under a dry oxide on thin SiGe

sample.paper: “The Si1XGeX layer thicknesses for the two wafers used were 80 nm and 70 nm for X = 0.15 and X = 0.20, respectively.”
sample.ours: COMPOSITION: Si0.85Ge0.15 or Si0.80Ge0.20; FILM recorded, read by no program
sample.note: Every SiGe program treats the alloy as infinite. At 150 min the 80 nm layer has lost about 26 nm of silicon-equivalent thickness to the oxide; Long's Figure 6 shows the layer nearly consumed into one Ge-rich layer.

sample.paper: “Epitaxial layers of Si1XGeX on a 100-nm Si buffer layer were grown on (100)-oriented Si substrates.”
sample.ours: ORIENTATION: Si100; buffer in FILM only

sample.paper: “The native oxides were not removed prior to oxidation.” 51 Å and 55 Å (legends); XPS finds oxidized germanium in it (Figures 1-2)
sample.ours: STARTING_OXIDE_NM: 5.1 / 5.5; CLEAN: not_stated (no clean; the vocabulary has no word for “native oxide kept”)
sample.note: Recorded, but neither SiGe program reads STARTING_OXIDE_NM: both start from a 1 nm hypothesis.

sample.paper: not stated (epitaxial on Si; pseudomorphic presumably)

history.item: Epitaxial Si1-xGex on a 100 nm Si buffer on (100) Si
history.paper: “Epitaxial layers of Si1XGeX on a 100-nm Si buffer layer were grown on (100)-oriented Si substrates.”; supplied by the NSE-IM2NP team and NanoTecMat platform (acknowledgments, PDF p. 10)
history.ours: COMPOSITION on the sample; the layer stack is recorded (FILM) and read by no program

history.paper: “The native oxides were not removed prior to oxidation.” Native oxide 51 Å (x = 0.15) and 55 Å (x = 0.20) by ellipsometry (Figure 6 and 5 legends)
history.ours: STARTING_OXIDE_NM on the sample; no SiGe program reads it (Rabie starts from 1 nm, the inventory from 1 nm)

history.paper: “The thermal oxidation was done using a tube furnace at ambient pressure flushed with dry O2”

history.ours: RUN RampUp DURATION 300 TEMP 600->900 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Five minutes from 600 °C in dry oxygen is ours; the paper states only the temperature and time at temperature.

history.paper: Figure legends: “900C-25min”; “tube furnace at ambient pressure flushed with dry O2 at 800 C, 850 C, 900 C, 950 C, and 1000 C”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 1500 TEMP 900->900 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Dry oxygen at 1 atm (“ambient pressure”); flow not stated.

history.ours: RUN RampDown DURATION 300 TEMP 900->600 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Five minutes down to 600 °C in dry oxygen is ours.

history.item: Ellipsometry (oxide), RBS 2 MeV He (Ge depth profile)
history.paper: “Oxide and pile-up layer thicknesses were determined by fitting simulated curves to the experimentally determined RBS spectra.”; ellipsometry at 632.8 and 830 nm, three-layer model, sample standard deviation 3.8 nm against RBS
history.note: The RBS depth resolution is not stated.

history.paper: “The XPS profiles show limited oxidized Ge in the native oxide, while no oxidized Ge is present in the thermal oxide”
history.ours: the inventory program puts none in the oxide; the Rabie program reports a GeO2 fraction of the oxide
history.note: The Rabie program's GeO2 fraction (4.6 to 13.6% at the end of these histories) contradicts the XPS.

steps.name: RampUp
steps.label: Push and heat-up (not described)
steps.isl: RUN RampUp DURATION 300 TEMP 600->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: not stated
steps.timing: not stated; 1 to 20 min searched

steps.name: Oxidation
steps.label: Dry oxidation, 850 °C, 75 min
steps.isl: RUN Oxidation DURATION 4500 TEMP 850->850 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: “oxidized at 850 C for 75 min” (Figure 2 caption)
steps.timing: time at temperature stated in the legends; whether it includes the push is not stated

steps.name: RampDown
steps.label: Pull and cool-down (not described)
steps.isl: RUN RampDown DURATION 300 TEMP 850->600 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: not stated
steps.timing: not stated; 1 to 20 min searched

steps.name: Measure
steps.label: Ellipsometry (oxide), RBS 2 MeV He (Ge depth profile), XPS with Ar+ etch
steps.paper: “Oxide and pile-up layer thicknesses were determined by fitting simulated curves to the experimentally determined RBS spectra.”; ellipsometry at 632.8 and 830 nm, three-layer model, sample standard deviation 3.8 nm against RBS
